area: platform and edges: Worker routing, auth, deletion jobs, lib, experiments and dev routes, core/durable, core/protocol, wrangler config, check-imports
purpose: Route each /api request to the right Durable Object by session user id, sign users in, delete an account completely and idempotently through a queue, and provide shared primitives (safe fetch, sealing, alarms, wire schema).
summary: Most of the platform layer is sound: every production DO name goes through lib/names.ts from the session user id, deletion steps are idempotent and tested, and crypto, hello-deadline and the import check are small and correct. One real gap blocks freezing: account deletion tombstones the user before jobs are queued, so a failed enqueue leaves data no retry can reach. The rest are small: a quadratic regex in html-text, unguarded experiment RPC on AgentDO, and dead experiment and history code.

subareas.name: Routing and socket upgrade
subareas.why: Origin check, session lookup before the stub, 5 s upgrade deadline and room id validation are right. Minor: every /api JSON body is read before routing (router.ts:35-37, 63).

subareas.name: Name construction (invariant 5)
subareas.why: Every production DO name is built here with checkUser/checkRoom/checkSlug. No production idFromName exists outside this file.

subareas.name: Auth and session
subareas.why: Tombstone check with a 30 s live cache, session revoke, dev sign-in with a second localhost guard (dev-session.ts:16-17). createAuth per request measured 0.14 ms in Bun (not workerd).

subareas.name: Account deletion route
subareas.why: Broken retry path: tombstone and DELETING land before jobs are queued (lines 66-68), and a tombstoned user gets 401 on retry (line 57).

subareas.name: Deletion job and queue consumer
subareas.why: Each step is safe to run twice, R2 deletes are prefix-scoped, the last room job finishes the account, dead deletions are requeued. Gaps: enqueue-side validation, batch size.

subareas.name: Durable helpers: alarm, safe-fetch, crypto, hello-deadline, wipe, hash
subareas.why: safe-fetch checks every redirect hop, blocks private IPv4 and IPv6, documents its DNS rebinding limit. crypto binds AES-GCM to user and provider, rotates by kek version. alarm.ts writes a wakeup history nothing in production reads.

subareas.name: HTML to text
subareas.why: Quadratic regex on hostile input (measured below). Reached from the agent web tool (up to 1 MB) and routine watches (256 KB), inside a DO with a 30 s CPU budget.

subareas.name: Experiments
subareas.why: Measurement harness wired into production AgentDO (agent-do.ts:6-7, 83-85, 672-673, 677-686). Its RPC has no NODE_ENV guard, unlike every other dev method. imports.ts is a one-off probe with no caller.

subareas.name: Dev routes and dev-only methods
subareas.why: Routes check NODE_ENV and localhost, and the production bundle drops the route branches (verified). But about 31 scattered NODE_ENV checks are the only guard, some routes take names from the request, and account dev routes skip the session check.

subareas.name: Wire schema and ids
subareas.why: Socket frames and routes decode with Effect schemas at the edge (room/socket.ts:31, user-do.ts:64). Branded ids. schema.ts is on a subpath, off the client's root import.

subareas.name: Import check and wrangler config
subareas.why: check-imports passes on this tree and matches the AGENTS.md layering rules. The deletion dead-letter loop is sound, but the consumer batch size is unset.

strengths: Invariant 5 holds for production: all DO names come from names.ts, the upgrade sets the user id header from the session, and router.ts rejects a request that carries a user id key (router.ts:63).

Deletion is ordered (tombstone, rooms, user, auth rows), each step is idempotent, R2 deletes stay under the user's prefix (delete-account.ts:67), and the last room job finishes the account (delete-account.ts:47).
Dead deletions go back to the main queue with a 15 min delay (consumer.ts:17-27). Other dead bodies are dropped.
Dev gating is compile-time. A bun build with NODE_ENV=production removes the dev route strings (api/experiments/turn, 'sign in first', seed-agent, /dev/session).

problems.title: A failed enqueue after the tombstone strands the account
problems.evidence: account-route.ts:66-68 runs revokeUser, beginDeletion and enqueueDeletion with no rollback. Line 57 answers 401 to a tombstoned user, and getSessionUser rejects every session of that user (auth.ts:68-70), so no retry reaches deleteAccount. delete-account.ts:96-103 sends in chunks, so a mid-send failure leaves some rooms unqueued; their deletion_rooms entries never clear, and the user and auth rows are never removed. No test throws from the send.
problems.fix: If enqueueDeletion throws, clear the tombstone and DELETING flag (add cancelDeletion to UserDO), return 503, and let the user retry. beginDeletion already repeats safely. Test a throwing send.

problems.title: html-text regexes go quadratic on hostile pages
problems.evidence: html-text.ts:151 /<[^>]*>/g takes 12,265 ms on 128 KB of '<' with no '>' (measured in Bun). /<[^<>]*>/g takes 0 ms. html-text.ts:147 takes 930 ms on 16k unclosed '<script>'. Callers: agent/extensions/web.ts:40 (up to 1 MB) and user/routines-wiring.ts:98 (256 KB). At 1 MB the first pattern alone exceeds the 30 s DO CPU limit.
problems.fix: Change line 151 to /<[^<>]*>/g. Bound the script pass with indexOf, or cap input before the regexes. Add a 1 MB '<' test.

problems.title: Experiment RPC on AgentDO has no dev guard, and the harness ships to production
problems.evidence: agent-do.ts:677-686: experimentTurn, experimentStatus, experimentCoalescing have no NODE_ENV check, unlike devClassic and the rest (lines 761-804). agent-do.ts:672-673 runs an experiment SQL probe on every production alarm. The NODE_ENV=production bundle keeps experimentTurn, experiment:events, countRows, measureTurn and FAUX. Only the Worker route (index.ts:89-90) guards them.
problems.fix: Guard the three methods like the other dev methods and drop the alarm probe. Delete experiments/ once section 21 is settled.

problems.title: Dev routes take names from the request and check only NODE_ENV or localhost
problems.evidence: account-route.ts:90-99 and 109-121 build user, room and agent stubs from the URL with no session check, and residue calls deleteAll (line 113). The only guard is localhost (line 46). experiments/turn.ts:27 builds an AGENT name from ?name=. experiments/coalescing.ts:102-108 has no session check. All of it is safe only while the compile-time define is 'production'.
problems.fix: Put every /api/dev and /api/experiments route behind one guard (NODE_ENV, localhost, session). Build names only through names.ts. Or delete the routes no suite uses.

problems.title: The deployed bundle takes NODE_ENV from the building shell
problems.evidence: wrangler 4.146.0 wrangler-dist/cli.js:184934 defines process.env.NODE_ENV as the shell's value, or 'production' on deploy. A shell with NODE_ENV=development bakes every dev route into a deployed Worker. There is no deploy script; deploy:dry inherits the same behavior.
problems.fix: Set NODE_ENV=production in the deploy and deploy:dry scripts.

problems.title: Request bodies are read in full before any size check
problems.evidence: router.ts:35-37 clones and reads the whole JSON body and checks the 1 MB cap after, for every /api path before matching (router.ts:63). account-route.ts:25-28 does the same before its 4 KB cap.
problems.fix: Check content-length before reading, or scan only the routes that need it.

problems.title: Deletion userId is unchecked at enqueue, and the dead-letter loop can drop a deletion
problems.evidence: account-route.ts:65-68 and delete-account.ts:96-99 pass session.user.id unchecked. checkUser (names.ts:17-20) would throw in the consumer, so the job cycles forever through the DLQ requeue (consumer.ts:21). wrangler.jsonc: kiko-jobs-dead has no dead_letter_queue, so after 100 failed requeues the deletion is dropped, against the comment that deletion never gives up.
problems.fix: Run checkUser at enqueue. Give kiko-jobs-dead a dead-letter queue or an alert.

problems.title: UNVERIFIED: deletion batches may exceed the Free subrequest budget
problems.evidence: wrangler.jsonc sets no max_batch_size on kiko-jobs, so the default of 10 applies. consume() runs the jobs in sequence in one invocation (consumer.ts:31-38), each making about 9 + agents calls (delete-account.ts:38-54). architecture 17.3 says Free allows 50 subrequests per invocation. Whether DO RPC counts toward that is not verified.
problems.fix: Set max_batch_size: 1 on kiko-jobs. It costs nothing and removes the question.

overengineering.title: Wakeup history table and trim
overengineering.evidence: core/durable/src/alarm.ts:22-25, 58-61, 67-71. The only reader is test/hardening-worker.ts:44. Production never calls history(), but each fired wakeup pays an extra row write, the binding Free limit (architecture 17.3).
overengineering.why: No production reader; its only production effect is a write per fired wakeup.

overengineering.title: measure-worker/ (Worker kiko-measure-p0-06)
overengineering.evidence: measure-worker/entry.ts 116 lines, quickjs-probe.ts 17, wrangler.jsonc 12. No reference in apps, core, docs or scripts. The measure CLI calls the main Worker's /api/experiments/turn.
overengineering.why: A leftover probe Worker with its own SpinDO. Nothing deploys or calls it.

overengineering.title: experiments/imports.ts and its route
overengineering.evidence: imports.ts:18-42 and index.ts:1, 54. It probes pi-ai OAuth imports for architecture section 21 item 6. No caller in cli, web or tests.
overengineering.why: A one-off probe. Record the result in architecture.md and remove it.

overengineering.title: Experiment harness inside production AgentDO
overengineering.evidence: turn.ts (127 lines) and coalescing.ts (110) are used by agent-do.ts 6-7, 70, 83-85, 672-686; count-rows.ts (31) too. The measure CLI and test/coalescing-worker.ts use them.
overengineering.why: Keep while section 21 measurements are in use. Once settled, delete the harness and its AgentDO hooks in one change.

overengineering.title: About 31 scattered NODE_ENV checks
overengineering.evidence: grep 'process.env.NODE_ENV' in apps/server/src gives 31 sites, each with its own throw or return. The miss at agent-do.ts:677-686 is the evidence one helper is needed.
overengineering.why: One devOnly() helper and one dev-route guard make the miss impossible. Do it when the next dev route is touched.

tests: Covered: delete-account.test.ts (failure at each step completes on retry; re-runs delete nothing), jobs.test.ts (retry delay, DLQ requeue, unknown job dropped), safe-fetch.test.ts, hardening.test.ts (hello deadline, upgrade 504, wakeup cap and history), web-tools.test.ts (htmlToText, basic), credentials.test.ts (seal/open), CLI account-delete suite (end to end). Not covered: enqueue failure after the tombstone (the main gap), originAllowed and carriesUserId, html-text on pathological input, the DLQ path for a deletion that keeps failing, experiment RPC guards. core/durable has no test directory; its tests live in apps/server/test.
